question_en: An organization is concerned it will be unable to continue to operate because it has run out of cash. This is an example of:
explanation_en: Solvency risk is the risk that an organization will not be able to operate because it ran out of cash. Credit risk is the risk that a counterparty will not fulfill its contractual obligations. Liquidity risk is the risk that an asset will be sold at a loss at a price below the asset's underlying fair value due to the market conditions at the time of the sale.

question_en: The standard deviation of returns for a portfolio of risky assets is:
option_a: less than the standard deviation of the least risky asset.
option_b: greater than the standard deviation of the least risky asset.
option_c: less than or equal to the standard deviation of the most risky asset.
explanation_en: The standard deviation of return of a portfolio of many risky assets can be less than or greater than the standard deviation of the least risky asset, depending on the correlations of returns among the assets and their weights in the portfolio. However, the portfolio standard deviation must be less than or equal to the standard deviation of the most risky asset.

question_en: In assessing the pricing power of companies in an industry using Porter's five forces, an analyst will most likely determine that companies have less pricing power when:
option_b: the threat of substitute products is low.
option_c: switching costs for consumers are high.
explanation_en: When barriers to entry are low, the threat of new entrants is high; it is easier for new companies to enter into the industry. This potential competition decreases the pricing power of companies currently in the industry. Low threat of substitute products and high switching costs for consumers tend to increase the pricing power of companies in an industry.

question_en: The portion of a hedge fund's return that is attributable to its exposure to specific sectors is its:
explanation_en: Strategy beta is the return attributable to a fund's sector exposures. Alpha is the return attributable to a fund's security selection. Market beta is the return attributable to a broad market index.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 3 - Answers.pdf
question_en: A real estate fund manager that specializes in property development is most likely to structure itself as a(n):
explanation_en: Finite-life, closed-end funds are appropriate for riskier real estate investment strategies such as development, redevelopment, repositioning, and leasing. Indefinite- life, open-end funds often focus on core real estate strategies that provide steady cash flow from well-leased, high-quality commercial and residential real estate in desirable markets.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 3 - Answers.pdf
question_en: Institutional investors in alternative assets are most likely to progress from:
option_a: direct investing to co-investing to fund investing.
option_b: direct investing to fund investing to co-investing.
option_c: fund investing to co-investing to direct investing.
explanation_en: As an institutional investor starts investing in alternative investments, they often start with fund investing because they can rely on the expertise of the fund manager. Next, they may often progress to co-investing so they can learn from the expertise of the fund manager. Then, the institutional investor may apply what they have learned and acquire alternative investments directly.

question_en:
An equal-weighted index has a value of 100 at the beginning of a period. The five securities that make up the index have the following prices for the period:

| Security | Beginning price | Ending price |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 20 | 22 |
| 2 | 80 | 72 |
| 3 | 130 | 143 |
| 4 | 250 | 225 |
| 5 | 320 | 352 |

The index value at the end of the period is:
explanation_en: The return on an equal-weighted index for a period is a simple average of the returns on its constituent securities. The returns on the five securities are +10%, –10%, +10%, – 10%, and +10%. The index return is (10%, – 10%, + 10%, – 10% + 10%) / 5 = 2% and the index value is 100 × 1.02 = 102.

question_en: Which of the following investors typically have the lowest need for liquidity?
explanation_en: Defined benefit pension plans pay out predetermined amounts to beneficiaries. These are long-term in nature and sponsoring entities have enough time to plan out their distributions such that liquidity needs are rarely pressing. Banks and mutual funds have significant liquidity needs, as their customers or investors may liquidate their holdings at any time.

question_en: An investor holds a bond with a duration gap of +1. If the investor expects interest rates to immediately rise, selling the bond at the end of the investor's investment horizon would result in a:
explanation_en: A positive duration gap indicates that the bond's Macaulay duration is higher than the investor's investment horizon. In this case, price risk dominates and the investor would experience a loss on the bond.

question_en: Infrastructure projects are most likely characterized by high:
option_c: correlations of returns with public equities.
explanation_en: Because they involve long-term contracts and typically high barriers to entry, infrastructure projects tend to provide stable cash flows that are relatively non-cyclical, and returns that exhibit low correlations with public equity markets.

explanation_en: The theory that bearing unsystematic risk will provide no additional expected return assumes that unsystematic risk can be diversified away at no cost.

question_en: During which stage of a portfolio company's development does a venture capital fund provide it with capital to prepare it for an initial public offering?
explanation_en: The mezzanine stage refers to the timing of the financing, which occurs when a company is preparing to go public. The "later stage" happens after production and sales have begun, but prior to going public. The formative stage is early in a company's development.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 3 - Answers.pdf
question_en: An organization's risk management process is least likely to:
explanation_en: The risk management process seeks to (1) identify the organization's risk tolerance, (2) identify and measure the risks that the organization faces, and (3) modify and monitor these risks. The process does not seek to minimize or eliminate all of these risks. Because organizations and investment portfolios earn returns above the risk-free rate by taking on risk, they should not avoid risk.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 3 - Answers.pdf
question_en: An economist determines that Argove Industries is a low-cost producer in its industry. As a result, the economist should expect that Argove can earn returns:
option_a: only at its cost of capital.
option_b: above its cost of capital both in the short run and long run.
option_c: above its cost of capital in the short run, but not in the long run.
explanation_en: A low-cost producer in an industry can earn both short-run and long-run returns above its cost of capital even in a competitive industry, as long as it can sustain its cost advantage relative to its competitors over time.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 3 - Answers.pdf
question_en: A portfolio manager is reviewing the performance of a portfolio and calculates the Treynor measure to be 4.29. The analyst should interpret this measure to mean that the portfolio:
option_a: has more risk than the market.
option_b: outperformed the market based on systematic risk.
option_c: achieved 4.29% higher returns than a portfolio on the Security Market Line with the same level of systematic risk.
explanation_en: The Treynor measure expresses excess return per unit of systematic risk. The portfolio does not necessarily have more risk than the market. The percentage portfolio return above that of a portfolio with the same beta that lies on the SML is measured by Jensen's alpha, not the Treynor measure.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 3 - Answers.pdf
question_en: Aros Funds manages a family of mutual funds and employs a team of fundamental analysts, who research firms by analyzing financial statements and SEC filings. Under which form(s) of the efficient market hypothesis (EMH) would Aros Funds have the potential to achieve positive risk-adjusted returns consistently using fundamental analysis?
option_c: No form of the EMH is consistent with earning positive risk-adjusted returns using fundamental analysis.
explanation_en: Fundamental analysis (i.e., analysis of public non-market data) can produce positive risk-adjusted returns if markets are weak-form efficient but not semistrong-form efficient. Under the semistrong form of the EMH, fundamental analysis cannot consistently achieve positive risk-adjusted returns.

question_en: An investor in a sponsored depository receipt (DR):
option_a: holds the voting rights for the DR shares.
option_b: must obtain the foreign currency in which the DR is traded.
option_c: should be familiar with market procedures and regulations in the DR issuer’s country.
explanation_en: In a sponsored DR, voting rights of the shares are held by the investor. In an unsponsored DR, voting rights are retained by the depository bank. An advantage of DR shares over direct investments in foreign companies is that DR shares trade in the investor's domestic market and currency.

question_en: Which of the following mortgage-backed securities is most likely to feature credit tranching?
explanation_en: Commercial mortgage-backed securities often feature credit tranching in which subordinated tranches are the first to absorb credit losses. Sequential-pay CMOs employ time tranching in which all principal payments flow to Tranche 1 up to its principal amount, then to Tranche 2 up to its principal amount, and so on. Agency RMBS are pass-through securities and do not feature credit tranching or time tranching.
